title: Beyond load shedding: how South Africa’s electricity crisis scarred industry and deepened deindustrialisation
summary: Load shedding has ended, but the damage to manufacturing has not. Drawing on two studies in Energy Policy and Energy Economics, the authors show that outages cut jobs, postponed investment and cost export opportunities, and argue that restoring power does not restore lost capabilities.
keyPoints: Firms cut jobs, delayed investment, bought costly backup power and lost export opportunities.
Repeated interruptions broke the continuity manufacturing employment depends on.
Ending load shedding is only the beginning: electricity must be treated as productive infrastructure.
